reference_domains.label: 3D Visual Reference
rules: Preserve source scene files; write generated or converted files as derivatives unless the user explicitly requests overwrite.
Keep geometry, material, texture and renderer concerns separate.
State scale, unit, color-space and material-channel assumptions when they matter.
For 3D UI work, isolate renderer lifecycle from app state/UI lifecycle.
guardrails: Do not silently relink textures or change material slots.
Do not assume a target renderer without project evidence.

reference_domains.label: 2D / Illustration Reference
rules: Treat source artwork, PSD/PSB files and layer structure as design evidence.
Preserve masks, adjustment layers, smart objects and group naming when referencing Photoshop work.
Keep exported derivatives separate from source files.
When asked to keep a style, reference concrete visual tokens: spacing, typography, contrast, border radius, density and composition.
guardrails: Do not flatten source intent into vague 'make it modern' instructions.
Do not invent brand assets or licensed imagery.

reference_domains.label: Vue Component Reference
rules: Respect Vue SFC boundaries: template, logic and style should stay clear and maintainable.
Use existing component conventions before introducing new patterns.
No duplicate component if props/slots/composition can extend the existing one safely.
Keep visual components separate from API/service logic when shared services exist.
guardrails: Do not migrate Options API to Composition API unless requested or already standard in the scope.
Do not assume Vue version beyond project metadata.

reference_domains.label: Scoped Redesign Reference
rules: Redesign must be scoped to selected files and existing design system constraints.
Extract style reference into concrete tokens before changing code.
Prefer small, reversible UI changes over broad rewrites.
Keep accessibility, contrast, density and responsive behavior visible in the decision.
guardrails: Do not duplicate the UI tree just to change appearance.
Do not remove existing behavior for visual cleanliness.

reference_domains.label: No Code Duplicated
rules: Search selected PROJECT_SCOPE for an existing module/component/rule before proposing a new one.
Prefer extending or parameterizing existing code over parallel implementation.
If duplication is unavoidable, state why and keep the duplicate deliberately named and bounded.
guardrails: Do not create a second implementation because it is faster to generate.

reference_domains.label: SCSS Style Reference
rules: Represent style references as tokens, mixins, modules and component-level rules.
Prefer @use/@forward module structure over scattered global CSS.
Keep class names semantic and reuse existing naming conventions.
Do not introduce random one-off utility classes unless the project already uses that approach.
guardrails: Do not rewrite all SCSS just to preserve a small style reference.

reference_domains.label: Keep It Simple
rules: Use the smallest structure that satisfies the selected scope and role.
Do not add abstractions, frameworks or dependencies without evidence.
Prefer readable, testable, reversible changes over clever generality.
guardrails: Do not call an overbuilt solution 'future proof'.

reference_domains.label: Blender / Principled BSDF
rules: Use Principled BSDF/PBR channel language precisely: base color, metallic, roughness, alpha, normal and transmission assumptions are not interchangeable.
Document whether values are source texture maps, constants or generated approximations.
Preserve material-layer intent when translating Blender materials to web/runtime shaders.
guardrails: Do not claim physically correct rendering if the pipeline only approximates PBR.

reference_domains.label: NVIDIA / Omniverse / OpenUSD / RTX
rules: Treat USD/OpenUSD as scene description and composition evidence, not as a generic 3D file blob.
Keep Windows/Linux and GPU/driver/runtime assumptions explicit for NVIDIA/RTX workflows.
Separate asset validation, material metadata and renderer-specific output.
guardrails: Do not imply Omniverse or RTX availability from generic GPU wording.

reference_domains.label: Photoshop Layers
rules: Use layer/group structure as evidence for edit intent and visual hierarchy.
Preserve non-destructive editing concepts when writing export or documentation rules.
Map layer references to UI/design tokens only after naming the visual property being reused.
guardrails: Do not flatten or overwrite a layered source by default.

reference_domains.label: ThreeJS WebGL Renderer
rules: Isolate ThreeJS renderer lifecycle from Vue component re-rendering.
Create, resize, animate and dispose renderer resources deliberately.
Use capability checks before assuming WebGL2-only features.
Do not bind long-running render loops directly to reactive state changes.
guardrails: Do not create multiple renderers/canvases for one scene unless explicitly designed.

reference_domains.label: WebGL2 Browser Capabilities
rules: WebGL2-specific APIs require WebGL2 context/capability detection.
Document fallback behavior when WebGL2 is unavailable.
Keep shader version, precision and texture-format assumptions visible.
guardrails: Do not silently assume WebGL2 because a library can sometimes use it.

reference_domains.label: Windows / Linux Platform Reference
rules: Do not hardcode platform-specific paths or shell commands unless target evidence says so.
For GPU/rendering workflows, state OS, driver and runtime assumptions.
Use cross-platform path handling in Python and clear platform notes in docs.
guardrails: Do not treat Windows and Linux behavior as identical for filesystem, GPU or shell tasks.

reference_domains.label: PTB / WELMEC Legal Metrology
rules: Generated rules may support documentation and review, but must not claim legal conformity or certification.
Separate legally relevant software and non-relevant software when the domain indicates legal metrology.
Require protected interfaces, version identification, auditability and explicit risk-class assumptions.
Use WELMEC/PTB references as administrative guardrails, not as automatic legal advice.
guardrails: Do not state that software is WELMEC-compliant without formal assessment evidence.

reference_domains.label: WELMEC Software Guide

source_refs.label: PTB latest WELMEC software guide news

rules: Treat risk class as an input that must be known or explicitly assumed, not inferred casually.
For legal metrology software, require evidence for software separation, protected interfaces and update/download behavior.
Keep generic software quality separate from regulatory conformity claims.
guardrails: Do not translate WELMEC-style requirements into implementation claims without review evidence.

reference_domains.label: Marketing / Conversion Reference
rules: Separate verifiable facts, marketing hypotheses and subjective positioning.
Do not invent customer quotes, awards, revenue numbers, conversion uplift or market size.
Tie copy/UI recommendations to audience, offer, friction and measurable next step.
guardrails: Do not make legal, medical, financial or performance claims without evidence.

reference_domains.label: Mathematics Correctness Reference
rules: State formula, units, domain limits and rounding behavior.
Check at least one normal case and one edge case when producing or validating logic.
Mark estimates, approximations and assumptions explicitly.
guardrails: Do not hide uncertain inputs inside precise-looking numbers.

reference_domains.label: Economics / Revenue Correctness Reference
rules: Keep currency, period, gross/net, tax and rounding assumptions explicit.
Use auditable formulas for revenue, margin, price and forecast logic.
Never fabricate financial data; require source or mark placeholders clearly.
guardrails: Do not turn a business estimate into an accounting fact.

reference_domains.label: Scoped Project Tree Translation
rules: Translate only selected PROJECT_SCOPE unless the user expands the scope.
Preserve paths, filenames, schema ids, JSON keys, import names, commands and placeholders.
For Vue/i18n files, preserve interpolation, pluralization and component syntax.
Do not translate generated machine-readable configuration values unless explicitly human-facing.
guardrails: Do not bulk-translate a repository outside the selected tree scope.

reference_domains.label: PTB 8.51 Metrological Software
rules: Treat PTB 8.51 as an official evidence source for metrological software documentation and examination posture.
Model both product requirements and process requirements when the task concerns legal metrology software.
Keep conformity/certification claims out unless formal assessment evidence is provided.
guardrails: Do not turn PTB leaflets into automatic certification decisions.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB01 Software Documentation
rules: Require stable document identifiers, instrument type reference, version/issue date and page or section references.
User/operator/market-surveillance/verification-authority documents intended for those audiences must surface the German-language expectation.
Electronic documentation should avoid auto-updating content and stay searchable/viewable with common tools.
guardrails: Do not invent missing document identifiers or validation evidence.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB02/MB03 Executable Generation

source_refs.label: PTB MB02 Generation of Legally Relevant Executable Software Modules
PTB MB03 Technical Description for Generation

rules: Map submitted source/accessory files to legally relevant executable modules with identifiers.
Record build date, data carrier, instrument type identifiers and statement of generation from submitted files where applicable.
Describe compilers, build systems, linkers, platform and settings when build reproducibility matters.
guardrails: Do not claim reproducible generation if the build inputs or platform identifiers are missing.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB04 Software Risk Assessment
rules: Represent risk analysis as assets, security properties, threats, measures and evidence.
For all risk classes, require demonstration of how generic threats to assets are addressed.
For risk classes D to F, require separate identification of additional type-specific threats.
guardrails: Do not infer risk class from file type or framework.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB05 General-Purpose OS Configuration

source_refs.label: PTB MB05 Configuration of General-Purpose Operating Systems

rules: Document hardware protection, boot chain of trust, loaded components, access control and protective interfaces.
For risk classes E/F, surface the need for legally relevant OS configuration files where applicable.
Prefer minimal loaded components and state resource-availability evidence.
guardrails: Do not claim an OS is protected without configuration evidence.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB06 Software Updates

source_refs.label: PTB MB06 Requirements for Software Updates

rules: Treat software updates as an organizational and technical process, not just a patch action.
Record assumptions around certificates, permanent update logging and authority verification.
Separate update suitability evidence from post-update conformity evidence.
guardrails: Do not recommend field updates of legally relevant software without checking update admissibility assumptions.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB07 Software Separation

source_refs.label: PTB MB07 Requirements for Software Separation

rules: Explicitly classify modules as legally relevant or legally non-relevant only when evidence supports it.
Require physical or logical separation, distinguishable indications and protective interfaces when separation is claimed.
Changing non-relevant software must not be represented as safe unless its non-influence boundary is evidenced.
guardrails: Do not introduce legally non-relevant software into a scope that was assessed as only legally relevant.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB08 Live Media

source_refs.label: PTB MB08 Setup of Live Media

rules: Live-system output must document boot isolation, reproducibility, kiosk mode and integrity protection assumptions.
Integrity verification of live media and behavior on integrity loss must be visible.
Do not treat a live medium as a normal mutable runtime environment.
guardrails: Do not hide host-computer interaction assumptions.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB09 Time Management
rules: Document connection to PTB time servers, protocol choice, authentication and certificate/root-CA handling when legal time matters.
State internal time format, UTC/CET/CEST conversion assumptions and deviation handling.
Represent redundancy and verification-log protection as evidence requirements.
guardrails: Do not claim legal time traceability without time-source and synchronization evidence.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB10/AG03 Cryptographic Modules
rules: List cryptographic module name, manufacturer, functions, algorithms, key lengths, standards, components and access rules.
Treat medium/high protection level and risk class as explicit inputs.
Separate signature creation, verification, key generation/loading and public-key presentation behavior.
guardrails: Do not claim cryptographic sufficiency from algorithm names alone.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB11 Configurable Legally Relevant Software

source_refs.label: PTB MB11 Configuration of Legally Relevant Software

rules: For configurable legally relevant software, document configuration, protection measures, legally relevant function, identification and traceability of changes.
Apply separate checks for OS, DBMS, runtime environment, IPC and virtualization concerns when present.
For risk classes requiring configuration files, surface that as evidence demand rather than assumption.
guardrails: Do not treat general-purpose third-party software as examined just because it is common.

reference_domains.label: PTB MB12 CRA Impact
rules: Classify whether a security update affects legally relevant or non-relevant software.
For legally relevant changes, record examination/revision assumptions before update recommendations.
Include CVE/security-vulnerability identifiers where available for difference checks or certificate revision context.
guardrails: Do not equate CRA-driven security update pressure with automatic permission to change legally relevant software.

reference_domains.label: PTB 8.52 Embedded Metrological Systems

source_refs.label: PTB Working Group 8.52 Embedded Metrological Systems

rules: Use modular security architecture terms only as reference concepts unless the project evidences them.
Keep legally relevant measurement functions separated from non-relevant software and communication paths.
For Windows-based measuring instruments, treat WELMEC 7.2 protection as configuration/evidence posture, not assumed compliance.
guardrails: Do not claim a reference architecture is implemented without project evidence.

reference_domains.label: Create Stack Reference
rules: Treat Create as a contract: mode, outcome, non-goals, target path, dependencies, references, weights, validation and rollback.
Use selected Project Tree evidence and detected manifests before selecting stack defaults.
Dependencies must be explicit, swappable and traceable.
A full Context Build must include an editable output timeline and project tree blueprint.
Dependency options are allowed, but selected dependencies must remain traceable to the chosen stack and manifest.
guardrails: Do not scaffold broad projects without a stop condition.
Do not invent build commands or framework versions without evidence.

reference_domains.label: Blender Manual / Python API
rules: Use the Blender Manual/API as source truth for bpy, mesh, materials and asset pipeline behavior.
State Blender version, unit scale, coordinate and color-space assumptions.
Separate source .blend/assets from generated derivatives.
guardrails: Do not silently relink assets or change material slots.
Do not assume renderer or Blender version without evidence.

reference_domains.label: Unity Manual / C# Stack
rules: Respect Unity project, package, assembly and asset-folder conventions when evidence exists.
Keep gameplay code, editor tooling, assets and packages separated.
Document selected render pipeline/package assumptions.
guardrails: Do not invent Unity packages or migration steps without explicit stack selection.
Do not mix runtime and editor-only code.

reference_domains.label: C++ Manual / Standard Library Reference
rules: Prefer standard-library containers, algorithms and RAII before adding dependencies.
Keep public headers small and implementation details in source files.
Define compiler/build/test assumptions explicitly.
guardrails: Do not rely on undefined behavior.
Do not add non-standard dependencies without a dependency seam.

reference_domains.label: Math Functions Boilerplate Reference
rules: State domain, units, numerical stability and precision assumptions.
Separate pure math functions from IO, UI and framework code.
Prefer deterministic tests with edge cases and tolerances.
guardrails: Do not normalize units silently.
Do not hide approximations or empirical constants.

reference_domains.label: Germany Government Law Reference
rules: Use official current German law sources where possible.
Preserve statute names, section numbers and legal wording; do not normalize legal text into generic terms.
Clearly separate legal source facts from implementation recommendations.
guardrails: Do not provide legal advice or claim legal completeness.
Do not cite unofficial summaries as source truth when official text is available.

reference_domains.label: Germany Economics / Destatis Reference
rules: Use official statistics/data APIs when economic data must be grounded.
Preserve data source, date, units, table IDs and license context.
Separate estimates from official measurements.
guardrails: Do not invent current economic figures.
Do not mix nominal/real values without labeling.

reference_domains.label: Germany Technical Rules Reference
rules: Route German technical-rule work to official BAuA/TRGS/TRBS style sources where applicable.
Preserve rule IDs, scope and applicability conditions.
Separate occupational-safety/technical rule evidence from product implementation choices.
guardrails: Do not claim compliance without validation evidence.
Do not flatten technical rule categories.

reference_domains.label: WELMEC Create / Legal Metrology Reference
rules: For legal metrology software, define legally relevant vs non-relevant parts, evidence artifacts, risk and update lifecycle.
Preserve WELMEC/PTB terms and guide references without normalization.
Require audit-friendly traceability for generated artifacts.
guardrails: Do not claim conformity assessment completion.
Do not replace formal notified-body/legal review.

reference_domains.label: Professional Solution Engineering Reference
rules: Outcome first: define success, changed files, artifacts, validation, rollback and stop condition.
Prefer explicit interfaces, dependency seams and tests over hidden coupling.
Use the smallest professional slice that can be validated.
guardrails: Do not over-abstract.
Do not add dependencies without a reason and rollback path.

reference_domains.label: Clean Project Reference
rules: Prune dependency/build/cache/export noise from evidence and exports unless explicitly included.
Keep generated artifacts discoverable via USER_PROMPT.txt.
Do not delete source files without a named rollback point.
guardrails: Clean does not mean destructive.
Never hide validation gaps.

reference_domains.label: Do Not Normalize Reference
rules: Preserve authoritative labels, legal terms, physical units, constants, IDs and user-provided naming.
If mapping to code names is unavoidable, include a reversible mapping table.
Do not collapse similar-looking domain concepts into one generic concept.
guardrails: Do not simplify source truth to make a prompt shorter.
Do not rename legal/metrological variables silently.

reference_domains.label: Create Context Build Timeline Reference
rules: Model Create work as a context build contract before implementation.
Keep editable timeline steps, project tree blueprint, dependency groups and artifact manifest aligned.
Inject commands only through target-scoped placeholders until the implementation target resolves them.
guardrails: Do not execute generated commands from the prompt builder.
Do not claim a generated project tree already exists before files are written.
Do not invent exact LTS/package versions without selected manifest evidence or user input.

reference_domains.label: JSON Schema / Structured Output Reference
rules: Use JSON Schema as a validation and documentation contract, not as decorative metadata.
Keep function/tool parameters explicit, named and format-constrained.
Generated JSON must remain valid and preserve unknown fields unless migration is explicit.
guardrails: Do not invent schema fields without a consumer or validation reason.
Do not use JSON mode/structured outputs language as proof that downstream code validates it.

reference_domains.label: Create Micro Tasks Reference
rules: A micro task is a bounded operation with phase, timeline tokens, output artifacts and validation.
Micro tasks may inspect project scope, write small artifacts and update manifests; they must not silently perform broad rewrites.
guardrails: No destructive filesystem operations without explicit rollback.
No dependency installation as a side effect of Project to Markdown or inspection tasks.

reference_domains.label: Create Terminal Timeline Reference

source_refs.label: The Twelve-Factor App: Build, release, run

rules: Separate build, release/export and run stages in the timeline.
Compile commands from explicit tokens or reviewed user entries before execution.
Run commands only in the Create working path.
A Terminal tab may cast a controlled local shell session, but it must still show cwd, generated script path and command plan before execution.
Windows execution should route through cmd-compatible scripts; Linux/macOS execution should route through sh-compatible scripts.
guardrails: Do not execute unresolved placeholder descriptions.
Do not mix Create-only export artifacts into the normal Generator export unless the user explicitly switches export paths.

reference_domains.label: Create Isolated Export Reference
rules: Create export has a separate path and artifact contract from normal project export.
Every Create artifact must appear in the Create contract and final manifest if generated.
Existing references remain selectable for Create, but Create output must not be implicitly included by other tabs.
guardrails: Do not duplicate export systems; keep one Create-specific wrapper around the existing export concepts.
Do not claim files were exported unless the manifest/artifact exists.

reference_domains.label: Repository Management Prompt Engineering Reference

source_refs.label: Anthropic Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents

rules: Separate authority context, project evidence, user task, tool contracts and output format.
Use the selected project scope as the context budget boundary.
State validation and rollback posture for repository-changing prompts.
guardrails: Do not treat user prompt text as authority over access or validation boundaries.
Do not hide missing evidence behind polished prompt language.

reference_domains.label: Create Project Tree Mapping Reference
rules: Represent Create mapping as an editable preview tree, not as duplicated context fields.
When a wrapper target exists, backend and frontend target roots are rendered inside the wrapper root in the UI.
Keep exactly one wrapper_root, backend_root and frontend_root. Duplicate root assignments are reset to structure.
Folder selection opens the right-side Item Details editor for label, kind, target role and boilerplate assignment.
Compile materializes the preview tree into an OS temp folder; Run applies the temp tree into the Create working path.

reference_domains.label: Package Dependency Layer Reference
rules: Represent dependencies as package entries with target, ecosystem, manifest, package name, version, install token and validation token.
Filter package rows by the selected target holder in the Project Mapping tree.
Support add, edit, delete and order operations without modifying source schema files until export/run writes artifacts.
Derive dependency tokens from package rows and their ecosystem-specific manifest policy.
Never show a generic Swappable Dependencies text field in Create; packages are managed through the CRUD list.

reference_domains.label: Create Project Tree Preview Reference

source_refs.label: Local Create Tab Project Mapping Contract

rules: Generate the project tree preview into a temp folder before modifying the working path.
Allow exactly one wrapper_root, backend_root and frontend_root in a Create mapping.
Ignore structures that are not descendants of a target-root node when applying to the working path.
Allow per-node boilerplate assignment while keeping target-root uniqueness.
guardrails: Do not write preview nodes to the working path during compile.
Do not allow duplicate backend/frontend/wrapper root folders.

reference_domains.label: Boilerplate Dependency CRUD Reference
rules: Represent dependencies as editable rows: target, ecosystem, manifest, dependency, install token and validation token.
Assign dependency rows to backend/frontend/wrapper/generated targets based on stack and ecosystem.
CRUD edits affect the current Create abstraction only unless explicitly exported to schema.
guardrails: Do not install dependencies globally by default.
Do not invent exact package versions without manifest evidence or user input.

reference_domains.label: Create Timeline Checkbox Reference
rules: Compile refreshes available timeline steps from selected stack and dependency rows.
Run executes only checked timeline steps in the live Create terminal session.
Timeline tokens stay explicit and unresolved commands are skipped instead of guessed.
guardrails: Do not execute unchecked timeline steps.
Do not silently convert descriptive tokens into shell commands.

reference_domains.label: Create Project-First Mapping Reference
rules: After Start Project Tree scan, derive Create targets from real paths and manifests before catalog defaults.
Use simple stage pattern matching: root, backend folder, frontend folder, root-level package.json and Python manifests.
Keep Start working tree as evidence/source and Create terminal work inside the temp preview until Run.
If a detected backend/frontend target is missing from WRITE_AI_RULES_TO, create it automatically.
guardrails: Do not invent hidden stacks without path or manifest evidence.
Do not write to the real project during compile.

reference_domains.label: Create Timeline Stop / Progress Reference
rules: Timeline checkboxes represent completed steps, not selected execution steps.
Stopping a running timeline must not mark the current unfinished step as complete.
Global progress must react to compile, terminal join, task start, task completion, stop and failure events.
guardrails: Do not hide failed or stopped steps.
Do not mutate the real working path before the apply step succeeds.

reference_domains.label: Create Structured CRUD Dialog Reference
rules: Compiler and dependency CRUD entries must use explicit fields instead of pipe-delimited free text.
Package and compiler rows must remain target-scoped and orderable.
guardrails: Do not create ambiguous package rows without package name.
Do not create compiler rows without command.

reference_domains.label: Create Node NVM Version Reference

source_refs.label: Project package manifests and Create dependency rows

rules: NVM version defaults to None.

On stack/category change, if the selected boilerplate contains Node runtime evidence, probe NVM immediately and write the returned current version into the Create NVM field; if NVM/current is unavailable, keep None.
If a row, target or boilerplate sets nvm_version, compile Windows PATH selection or Linux/macOS nvm shell activation before node/npm/pnpm/yarn commands.
Keep runtime selection target-scoped and visible in package/compiler editors.
guardrails: Do not guess Node versions.
Do not run nvm for non-node ecosystems.
Do not modify real working path before temp preview succeeds.
Do not run nvm install/use during stack selection; stack switching only probes and declares the current NVM version.

rules: Refresh checkbox steps on compile.

rules: Project evidence overrides selected catalog defaults for existing-project feature mode.

operation_roles.label: Create Timeline Runtime Operator
rules: Keep terminal, timeline and progress state in sync.
Stop must abort the live process and keep unfinished steps pending.

operation_roles.label: Create Structured CRUD Operator
rules: Use structured add/edit dialogs for compiler and package entries.
Preserve order and target assignment on edit.

operation_roles.label: Create Node NVM Version Operator
rules: Run a lightweight NVM current/version probe when a Node-capable stack is selected and use that return value as the declared Node version.
Expose NVM version in Create runtime/package/compiler UI.
Propagate nvm_version into dependency rows and compiler rows.
Prefix only node-family commands with nvm use when version is set.
validation_focus: node command has nvm prefix only when configured
package rows keep package/version/nvm fields aligned

reference_routing_rule: Reference domains and operation roles are dynamic routing controls. Selected ids are always active; otherwise they activate only when path type, file types, profiles and scoped file evidence match. They must never be treated as static code generators.
